Apple is developing a new option that allows iPhone users to erase their storage space more thoroughly when clearing their device, but with one limitation. Details below.

China-only exclusive new feature

Code references in today's release of iOS 27.2 beta 1 reveal a new iPhone erase option that allows users to overwrite the entire storage space of the device with empty data, including storage space that is not currently in use.

In addition to erasing iPhone data, this feature can also overwrite the device's entire storage space with empty data, including storage space that is not currently in use. Apple warns that this process may take longer than a standard erase and may affect the device's lifespan.

This move is quite interesting, because when users currently erase their iPhone, the device's encryption key is destroyed, effectively making residual data unreadable. In fact, Apple has clearly stated this in its Apple Platform Deployment support document:

While researching today's beta, 9to5Mac confirmed that under the current implementation, this feature is only available for iPhone models sold in China. Apple appears to have added this feature to comply with an upcoming data wipe regulation.

This is because a new Chinese standard taking effect on January 1, 2027, will require smartphones and other electronic devices to provide more thorough methods of erasing stored data, including through overwriting.

For semiconductor storage (such as flash storage used in smartphones), one of the approved methods is to overwrite the storage space containing user data with meaningless data at least once. This closely aligns with Apple's described practice of replacing storage space with empty data.

Finally, this new erase option is not exclusive to iPhone—the code also shows support for other devices, including iPad, HomePod, and Apple Vision Pro.
